- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤ 0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to avoid missing reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; cap forecast at 1–2% below true peak.
- Model underreacts to sentiment shifts in early periods (e.g., 1–3 days after sentiment change); delay adjustment by 1–2 days if sentiment flips.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons; if forecast is > 2% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.5%.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses late-period momentum; add 0.5–1.0% buffer if sentiment remains bullish at end of horizon.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; align forecast with sentiment peak 1–2 days ahead.
